source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A child spilled boiling water on his arm. The skin is red, moist, blistered and very painful. This is a:
questions.rationale: Second-degree burns involve epidermis and dermis: moist, blistered and painful. Third-degree is pearly white or leathery and painless.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Burn depth (PDF p. 499)
questions.quote: Second degree. Involves the dermis; moist surface; with blisters; painful.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why is a third-degree burn area painless?
questions.rationale: Full-thickness burns destroy the dermis and its nerve endings; surrounding partial-thickness areas still hurt.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Burn depth (PDF p. 499)
questions.quote: Third degree. Involves the subcutaneous layer; pearly white; no pain.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During the first 48 hours after a major burn, the client's hematocrit rises. This is because:
questions.rationale: In the emergent phase plasma leaks from vessels to interstitial spaces, causing hypovolemia and hemoconcentration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Shock phase (PDF p. 499)
questions.quote: Hemoconcentration, increased hematocrit. Plasma is lost into the interstitial compartment (ISC).

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which electrolyte finding is expected in the first 48 hours after an extensive burn?
questions.rationale: Damaged cells release potassium (hyperkalemia); sodium is trapped in edema fluid (hyponatremia).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Shock phase (PDF p. 499)
questions.quote: Hyperkalemia and hyponatremia. This results from release of potassium from damaged cells

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Three days after a burn, a client's urine output increases greatly. The nurse watches for:
questions.rationale: In the fluid remobilization phase fluid returns to vessels (hypervolemia, hemodilution) and potassium moves back into cells.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Diuretic phase (PDF p. 499)
questions.quote: Hypervolemia, hemodilution and decreased hematocrit occur.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A man rescued from a house fire has singed nasal hair and sooty sputum. The priority is:
questions.rationale: These signs suggest inhalation injury; airway edema can develop quickly, so airway comes first.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Burns management (PDF p. 511)
questions.quote: Assess for sooty sputum and singed hair in the nose and eye brows.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A woman's dress catches fire while cooking. She should be told to:
questions.rationale: Rolling smothers the flames; running feeds them with oxygen. A blanket also cuts off oxygen.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 First aid (PDF p. 511)
questions.quote: Running causes the oxygen in the environment to further ignite the flame.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse discovers a fire in a client's room. The first action is to:
questions.rationale: RACE: Rescue (remove the client), Alarm, Confine, Extinguish.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Fire safety (PDF p. 511)
questions.quote: R — emove the client A — ctivate the fire alarm. C — onfine the fire. E xtinguish the fire

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When using a fire extinguisher, the nurse aims the nozzle at the:
questions.rationale: PASS: Pull the pin, Aim at the base, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Fire safety (PDF p. 511)
questions.quote: A — im at the base of the flame

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: By the rule of nines, an adult with burns of the entire front trunk and the whole right arm has about what percent burned?
questions.rationale: Anterior trunk 18% + one arm 9% = 27%.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Rule of nines (PDF p. 512)
questions.quote: The Rule of 9's for determining percentage of burns

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A 60-kg adult has 40% burns. Using the Parkland formula (4 mL × kg × %), how much LR is given in the first 8 hours?
questions.rationale: 4 × 60 × 40 = 9,600 mL in 24 hours; half (4,800 mL) in the first 8 hours from the time of burn.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Parkland formula (PDF p. 515)
questions.quote: 4mls. LR x weight in kg. x % of burns

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The best guide that burn fluid resuscitation is adequate is:
questions.rationale: Urine output, vital signs, CVP and level of consciousness show perfusion; adults should make at least 30 mL/hour.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Fluid balance (PDF p. 512)
questions.quote: Urine output

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: For pain in a client with major burns, morphine is given by which route?
questions.rationale: Poor tissue perfusion makes IM and SC absorption unreliable; give IV and watch for respiratory depression (have naloxone ready).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Pain relief (PDF p. 512)
questions.quote: Administer Morphine Sulfate per IV as prescribed. Monitor the client for respiratory depression.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A burn client on mafenide (Sulfamylon) begins breathing fast and deep. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Mafenide can cause metabolic acidosis (shown by hyperventilation); it also stings on application.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Topical antimicrobials (PDF p. 513)
questions.quote: The medication may cause metabolic acidosis (usually manifested by hyperventilation).

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client receiving silver sulfadiazine on his burns needs which lab monitored?
questions.rationale: Silver sulfadiazine can cause leukopenia; monitor the CBC, especially WBC.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Topical antimicrobials (PDF p. 513)
questions.quote: Side effects are as follows: rash, leukopenia, nephritis. Monitor cbc, especially the wbc.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: When dressing burns of the hand, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Separate dressings prevent webbing and contractures; remove rings and splint in a functional position.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Wound care (PDF p. 513)
questions.quote: No two burn surfaces should be allowed to touch; touching can promote webbing of digits

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Before hydrotherapy for burn care, the nurse should:
options: Keep the client NPO for 24 hours
questions.rationale: Hydrotherapy and debridement are painful; premedicate so the drug peaks during the procedure.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Hydrotherapy (PDF p. 514)
questions.quote: Administer analgesic 15 to 30 minutes before hydrotherapy to promote comfort.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A skin graft taken from the client's own thigh is called an:
questions.rationale: Autograft is from self; allograft from another person; xenograft from an animal; isograft from an identical twin.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Skin grafting (PDF p. 514)
questions.quote: Autograft. The donor site comes from the self.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: After a skin graft to the leg, the nurse should:
options: Elevate and immobilize the graft site
questions.rationale: Immobilize, elevate and avoid pressure so the graft can adhere; remove exudate and watch for infection.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Graft site care (PDF p. 514)
questions.quote: Elevate and immobilize the graft site.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with severe burns is given a histamine-2 blocker. The purpose is to prevent:
questions.rationale: Major burns cause stress ulcers (Curling's ulcer); antacids and H2 blockers are given.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 GI support (PDF p. 515)
questions.quote: To prcvcnt stress ulcer (Curling's ulcer).

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The priority goal in the rehabilitation phase of burns is to:
questions.rationale: Pressure garments, splints and exercise reduce scarring and contractures; fluid and airway are early-phase goals.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 16 Rehabilitation (PDF p. 516)
questions.quote: The priority goal of rehabilitation among burns clients is to prevent or minimize scarring.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Shock is best defined as:
questions.rationale: Shock is inadequate blood flow and oxygen delivery to tissues; low BP is a late sign.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 Shock (PDF p. 525)
questions.quote: Shock is due to inadequate blood flow and oxygen delivery to the capillaries and tissues of the body.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which shock type follows a massive heart attack?
questions.rationale: Cardiogenic shock results from pump failure (MI, dysrhythmias, tamponade).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 Shock types (PDF p. 521)
questions.quote: Cardiogenic Shock. This results from decreased cardiac output, e.g., MI, dysrhythmias, CHF, cardiac tamponade.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with a new T4 spinal cord injury has BP 80/50 and pulse 52 with warm, dry skin. This is:
questions.rationale: Loss of sympathetic tone causes vasodilation with hypotension and bradycardia; other shocks cause tachycardia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 Shock types (PDF p. 521)
questions.quote: This results from generalized vasodilatation due to conditions affecting the medulla oblongata and SNS, e.g., spinal cord injury

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A 78-year-old diabetic with an infected toe has fever, confusion, BP 84/40, HR 110 and RR 32. This most likely indicates:
questions.rationale: Infection with hypotension and organ dysfunction (confusion) indicates septic shock; act fast with fluids and antibiotics.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 527)
questions.quote: Septic shock results from severe infection. Purulent drainage indicates presence of infection.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is an early sign of shock?
questions.rationale: Early sympathetic response causes restlessness, tachycardia, tachypnea and cool clammy skin; hypotension and anuria are late.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 Shock manifestations (PDF p. 522)
questions.quote: Restlessness, confusion Tachycardia; tachypnea

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Early in shock, a client breathes rapidly. The ABG is likely to show:
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation early in shock blows off CO2; later, lactic acid causes metabolic acidosis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 527)
questions.quote: excessive loss of carbon dioxide leads to respiratory alkalosis.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A hypotensive client in hypovolemic shock is best positioned:
options: Head lower than the trunk, steeply
questions.rationale: Modified Trendelenburg (flat with legs raised) improves venous return without pushing abdominal organs onto the diaphragm.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 Shock management (PDF p. 523)
questions.quote: Position: Modified Trendelenburg

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which complication of prolonged shock affects the kidneys?
questions.rationale: Poor renal perfusion causes acute tubular necrosis and kidney failure; monitor hourly urine output.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 MODS (PDF p. 522)
questions.quote: Kidneys. Acute tubular necrosis and renal failure.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client in shock starts oozing from IV sites and the gums. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: DIC is a part of multiple organ dysfunction in shock: clotting factors are used up, causing bleeding.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 17 MODS (PDF p. 522)
questions.quote: Blood. Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) occurs.
